opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Keith Mclaughlin (E032), Analyst, full-time employee, requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access (admin requires owning role; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E032 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note listed full-time; Security DB is authoritative here). Contractors with basic training max out at read; write requires advanced training. Recommend read.
reason: Security DB (authoritative) shows E032 is a contractor with basic security training, not a full-time employee. Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read access (write requires advanced training). The requested write level exceeds the maximum, so the maximum of read is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Keith Mclaughlin (E032) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes:
- HR agent says: Analyst, full-time employee, recommends write. Claims full-time employees may have up to write access.
- Security agent says: Security DB shows contractor with basic security training. HR note listed full-time, but Security DB is authoritative. Contractors with basic training max out at read. Write requires advanced training. Recommend read.

The two notes conflict. The Security agent says their DB is authoritative on employment type. So Keith is a contractor with basic security training.

Access policy:
- contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Keith is a contractor with basic training → max is read.

Requested level: write. That's above maximum (read). Policy says if requested level is above maximum, grant the maximum. So grant read.

Also never grant more than requested. Requested write, max read → grant read.

Submit decision: read.

Evidence: Security DB authoritative shows contractor with basic security training; contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.
